reviewSummary.compatibilityRiskCoverage: PARTIAL — topology compatibility observed, but cross-platform path canonicality not proved

findings.title: Run occurrence identity has no proved repository path-address safety contract
findings.problem: Explore correctly requires an independent Run occurrence identity and proposes persistence under .flowkit/runs/<delivery>/<change-root>/<action-occurrence>/, but it leaves occurrence identity opaque without identifying or proving the filesystem-address boundary. A caller-supplied occurrence/address containing traversal or path separators can escape the intended Change root or create alias/nested addresses, especially across POSIX and Windows semantics.
reviewEvidence: POSIX controlled counterexample: path join with ../022-review-explore resolves outside the Change root.
Windows controlled counterexample: path join with ..\022-review-explore resolves outside the Change root.
Windows controlled counterexample: nested\022-review-explore becomes multiple path segments even if treated as one opaque logical id.
Existing Explore risk R6 covers topology drift but not untrusted/canonical path-address construction or path aliasing.
requiredRevision: Add an explicit persistence/path-address risk covering traversal, slash/backslash separators, empty/dot segments, absolute/drive-qualified forms, and cross-platform aliases.
Separate logical Run occurrence identity from repository address/path-segment validation, or define an equivalent canonical path-safe occurrence representation.
Add controlled negative proof showing malformed/adversarial occurrence/address inputs fail closed on both POSIX and Windows path semantics while canonical current topology remains accepted.
Keep final RunId display/sequence allocation design open for Proposal; do not solve this by parsing lifecycle authority from a display string.
nonRequirements: No production implementation is required in revise-explore.
No database/WAL/scheduler/multi-Agent recovery design is required.
No final RunId string format needs to be chosen at Explore if path safety can be proved independently.

verifiedFacts: The exact supplied checkpoint archive SHA-256 matches the Author-declared base snapshot hash.
Detached Node 22.23.2 and pnpm 11.22.0 execute successfully.
Typecheck passes, domain tests pass 25/25, and repository-declared Prettier check passes.
OpenSpec remains at the intended Explore boundary: 0/4 formal artifacts, proposal ready, specs/design/tasks blocked.
Both existing canonical OpenSpec specs validate strict 2/2.
021 adds only the Explore scaffold/artifact, delivery activation, and its stable Run record; no production implementation is present.
Repeated semantic ActionIdentity cannot distinguish multiple review-explore occurrences; a separate Run occurrence identity is required.
Existing OwnerAuthorityFact round-trips through JSON with exact validator acceptance and malformed/extra fields fail closed.
Opaque JSON Result payload can be persisted without interpreting reviewer/verification/next-boundary semantics, preserving separation from later admission and Policy changes.
The repository already demonstrates repeated Action history under one Change root, so a second runtime storage tree is unnecessary.
limitations: This is Review Explore only; it is neither Verification PASS nor Owner authority.

The Author's execution-local proof hashes cannot be independently recomputed because raw proof is intentionally excluded from the handoff payload; reviewer evidence comes from independent reproduction.
The supplied checkpoint has no .git directory, so Git commit existence/byte equivalence was not independently verified.

The exact stable-transfer v4 contract artifact was not supplied; its declared hash was recorded but not independently opened. This is non-blocking because the repository topology relevant to this finding is directly observable.
Symlink/reparse-point hardening was not elevated to a blocker in this Explore review; RE-022-001 is limited to canonical logical-to-physical path addressing and traversal/alias safety.
